blocks.content: A Great Circle is the largest circle that can be drawn on a sphere, dividing it into two equal hemispheres and defining the shortest distance between any two points on its surface.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: A Great Circle is the largest possible circle that can be drawn on a sphere, created by a plane passing through the sphere's center.
The Equator is the only line of latitude (parallel) that forms a Great Circle.
All pairs of opposite meridians (e.g., 0° and 180°) combine to form complete Great Circles.
An infinite number of Great Circles can be drawn on a sphere.
Great circle routes represent the shortest distance between any two points on the Earth's surface and are widely used in air and sea navigation.
The Equator is the ONLY parallel of latitude that is a Great Circle; all other parallels are Small Circles.
Pairs of opposite meridians (e.g., 70°E and 110°W) together form a single complete Great Circle.
Aviation and maritime navigators use Great Circle routes (Orthodromes) to minimize flight time and fuel consumption.
